title: Erosion and the people of a river valley
body: In a hilly district, farmers noticed that each monsoon the fertile topsoil from their fields washed into the river, and their crop yields fell year after year. Downstream, the river cut into its banks and washed away part of a road and a few houses. On the coast, a popular beach became narrower, and local fishers said that their catch near the river mouth had changed. Village elders recalled that earlier generations built earthen bunds along the hillslopes and small check dams across streams, which slowed the water, let sediment settle and recharged the groundwater, much like the Zabo system of Nagaland. The panchayat is now planning to revive these practices.

title: A sudden flood in a Himalayan valley
body: In February 2021, a devastating flood struck the Chamoli district in Uttarakhand. People and livestock lost their lives, and buildings, roads, bridges and hydel projects were badly damaged. Villages were cut off. Students studying the event learnt that in high mountains, rising temperatures make glaciers melt rapidly, so glacial lakes grow larger and press against natural dams made of ice or loose moraine. Heavy snowfall, avalanches, landslides or earthquakes can weaken such a dam. When it gives way, a huge volume of water rushes down the valley within a short time, damaging everything in its path.
